caption:
Why did my skin change in my 40s?
Usually not because you stopped trying.

Three things move at roughly the same time. Collagen and dermal thickness decline. That decline tracks hormonal change rather than birthdays. And sun exposure from twenty years ago starts becoming visible in the same decade.

In postmenopausal women, skin collagen was measured declining about 1-2% per year, alongside skin thickness and bone mass at a similar rate. That is 1987 data, measured on thigh and forearm skin, in women already past menopause - most people in their forties are not there yet. It describes a direction, not your number.

What changes is not the menu. It is the sequence, and the timeline you judge it on. Expect slower. Protect before you correct. Ask what to do first rather than what to add.

What to do about hormones is a medical conversation, not a skincare one.

General education only.
